tweet_summary: A video captioned 'Can you believe this was made by nature?' shows a person cracking open a rock that reveals vibrant purple/red geode crystals; the latter part of the clip is AI-generated.
why_note_decision: The post presents the clip as a real natural geode ('made by nature'). The original note and numerous commenters identify a 'Veo' AI watermark and note the rock visibly changes shape after being split, indicating the reveal is AI-generated. Passing off AI-generated footage as a real natural phenomenon to a credulous audience is a checkable visual misrepresentation that warrants a note. (The AI media description in the input wrongly treats it as a genuine geode discovery — corroboration with the note and comments shows it is fake.)
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that the video (at least the crystal-reveal portion) is AI-generated/fake rather than a real natural geode. The strongest evidence is the visible 'Veo' (Google DeepMind) AI watermark in the corner and/or the rock changing shape/form between frames; a passing note should cite at least one concrete tell (watermark or morphing geometry), not just assert 'this is AI' unsupported. A note that treats the footage as a genuine natural geode, or that only vaguely says 'looks fake,' is weak. Linking the Veo model page or explaining the watermark strengthens it.
reference_note: The latter part of this video is AI-generated and fake. The “Veo” AI watermark is visible in the bottom-right corner, and the rock visibly changes shape after being split — this is not a real natural geode.    https://deepmind.google/models/veo/

fact_check.claim_verdict: Misleading: presented as a real natural geode but the reveal is AI-generated (Veo watermark; rock geometry morphs between frames), corroborated by the note and many commenters.
fact_check.notes: Cannot view the video directly. The AI media description in the cached input describes it as a genuine geode discovery (an example of the AI description being wrong); the original Community Note, the explicit 'Veo' watermark cited there, and 10/10 top comments calling it AI all corroborate that the footage is AI-generated. Media confidence kept lower because the verdict hinges on visual tells I can't independently inspect.

importance.lens_rationale: 6.5M views; low individual stakes but part of the broad 'AI slop passed off as reality' problem — building norms/tooling for labeling synthetic media has real epistemic-commons value as generative video proliferates.
